title: Potato, baked, peel eaten, with meat

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the skin left on is a nutritious dish where whole potatoes are roasted, keeping the skin, and then combined with boiled or fried meat (commonly beef, pork or chicken). The skin retains fiber and nutrients, while the meat adds protein and satiety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato skin contains more vitamin C and fiber than the flesh.
High‑heat baking creates a crisp crust and intensifies flavor.
Baking potatoes in their skins is a tradition in Russia, Germany and the United States.
Meat‑potato combos appear in many national dishes, such as Russian zapekanka or French gratin.
Potatoes are the world’s fourth most produced food after rice, wheat and corn.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide a steady release of energy thanks to slowly digestible starches.

items.title: Source of vitamin C and potassium
items.content: The skin preserves most of the vitamin C, while the tuber is high in potassium, supporting heart function.

items.title: High‑quality protein from meat
items.content: Added meat boosts complete protein content, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Fiber for digestion
items.content: Both the skin and meat fibers help maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low fat when using lean meat
items.content: Choosing lean cuts keeps the dish relatively low in saturated fat.

items.title: Fat and salt content in meat
items.content: Fatty cuts can raise calorie count and saturated fat intake.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Over‑browning can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen; avoid overly dark crusts.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Excessively salty meat can increase hypertension risk; monitor salt usage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the baked potato hot, split it open and top with pieces of boiled or fried meat, butter, herbs or spices. The skin is edible and adds a pleasant crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags and reheat in a 180 °C oven to restore the crisp crust.
